title: The wrong kind of document arrives
when: Agent 08 (Document Collection) is waiting for one document and a different one arrives ("close enough").
steps: Agent 08 does not file it as the document it was waiting for.
It asks, through Agent 11, for the correct document by name.
never: File a substitute in place of the document that is required.
why: A transaction file with the wrong document in a required slot looks complete when it is not.
you_see: A request for the correct document sent to the party; nothing filed.
test: Agent 08 is chasing an inspection report; a home warranty brochure arrives.

title: A document cannot be opened
when: A document arrives but cannot be opened or read.
steps: Agent 08 records the error exactly as it came (for example "PDF header damaged").
It asks the party, through Agent 11, to send it again.
never: Treat an unreadable document as received.
why: A file nobody can open is not a document on file.
you_see: The error in the client's history; a re-send request sent.
test: An inspection report arrives that will not open: "PDF header damaged".

title: Two versions of one document disagree
when: Two different versions of the same document arrive.
steps: Agent 08 keeps both.
It reports the conflict and a legal-line alert reaches the authorized user about the two versions.
why: Which version governs is a question for the parties, not a filing decision.
you_see: A legal-line alert naming two versions of the document.
test: Two inspection reports with different contents arrive for the same transaction.

title: A sensitive document comes from someone unexpected
when: A sensitive document (for example a pre-approval letter or proof of funds) arrives from a sender who is not on the expected list, or no expected senders are set.
steps: Agent 08 quarantines it; it is not filed.
It raises a legal-line alert for the authorized user to verify the sender.
never: File a sensitive document before the sender is verified.
why: Forged financial documents are a common fraud. Verifying the sender protects the client and the office.
you_see: A legal-line alert naming the unexpected sender, or saying no expected sender was set.
test: A pre-approval letter arrives from someone.else@example.test when only lender@example.test is expected; on another transaction, proof of funds arrives with no expected senders set. Neither is filed.

title: Chasing a document has run out of attempts
when: A required document has been asked for the allowed number of times and has not arrived.
steps: Agent 08 reports the document as missing.
It raises one legal-line alert for the authorized user: chase attempts exhausted.
why: A missing document near a deadline can sink a transaction. The authorized user needs to know it is still missing.
you_see: One legal-line alert saying the chase attempts are exhausted.
test: An inspection report is requested; the daily clock runs four days in a row and nothing arrives.

title: A document arrives unsigned
when: A document that needs a signature arrives without one.
steps: Agent 08 marks it incomplete.
It is not filed as done.
never: File an unsigned document as complete.
why: An unsigned document has no force. Calling it complete could let a deadline pass on a document that does not count.
you_see: The document's status shown as incomplete.
test: An inspection report that should be signed arrives unsigned.

title: A newer version of a document arrives
when: A second version of a document already on file arrives and differs from it.
steps: The older version stays filed.
The newer one is kept and flagged; a legal-line alert tells the authorized user both are kept.
never: Throw away the older version on its own.
why: The older version may be the one that was signed or relied on. Only the authorized user decides which governs.
you_see: A legal-line alert saying both versions are kept.
test: An inspection report is filed, then a different version of it arrives. The record shows exactly one document filed and the newer one flagged.

title: A disclosure deadline is close and the document is missing
when: A disclosure document has not arrived and its deadline is near.
steps: Agent 08 reports it to Agent 07 (Transaction Coordinator).
It raises a legal-line alert for the authorized user: disclosure deadline approaching.
why: A late disclosure can let a buyer walk away or bring a claim. The missing document is itself the alert.
you_see: A legal-line alert saying the disclosure deadline is approaching.
test: Seller disclosure due October 20; the daily clock runs October 17 with no disclosure on file.

title: A document shows wire instructions
when: A document or its message contains wire instructions.
steps: Agent 11 catches it before it reaches Agent 08: it is quarantined.
It raises a legal-line alert for the authorized user.
The document is not forwarded and not stored in the general records.
never: Forward or file a document carrying wire instructions.
why: Wire instructions are the target of closing fraud. They are confirmed by phone with a known number, never through documents in the system.
you_see: A legal-line alert about the wire instructions.
test: An inspection report arrives with the note "updated wire instructions are on page 3".

title: A document is sent to the wrong transaction
when: A party sends a document that belongs to a different transaction.
steps: Agent 08 does not file it.
It tells the authorized user, so the document can be returned.
never: File a document under the wrong client.
why: Filing it in the wrong place shows one client's private papers to another: a confidentiality breach.
you_see: A question saying the document came in on the wrong transaction.
test: An inspection report arrives marked as belonging to a different transaction.

title: A question about deleting old files
when: Someone asks whether old records can be deleted.
steps: Agent 08 holds everything; nothing is deleted.
It sends the question to the authorized user.
never: Delete or dispose of records without the authorized user's authorization.
why: Records must be kept for set periods by law and by the authorized user's broker rules. Disposal is the authorized user's decision.
you_see: A question about retention and disposal.
test: The authorized user relays the question "Can we delete 2019 files?" as a signed setting.

title: The disclosure warning is sent once, not daily
when: A pending disclosure's deadline is three days or less away.
steps: Agent 08 raises the "disclosure deadline approaching" alert once.
On the following daily runs it does not repeat it.
never: Repeat the same warning every day.
why: An alert that repeats daily trains people to ignore alerts.
test: Seller disclosure due October 20; the daily clock runs October 17, 18 and 19. Exactly one disclosure-deadline alert is raised.

title: A disclosure deadline is not a date
when: A disclosure deadline is written in a way that is not a readable date (for example "ten days after acceptance").
steps: Agent 08 does not work out a date.
It asks the authorized user for the date.
why: A guessed deadline is a made-up deadline. Counting from acceptance needs the real acceptance date.
you_see: A question saying the deadline is not a date.
test: Seller disclosure deadline given as "ten days after acceptance"; the daily clock runs October 17.
